instantiated_cells.justification: The only periodic spending/expense statement required by this subchapter is the principal’s expense statement due July 31 and January 31, not an annual lobbyist-filed report.
The statute requires semiannual principal expense statements and requires lobbyists only to provide information to the principal, not monthly lobbyist spending reports.
No separate lobbyist spending report cadence is specified because spending reports are filed by principals, with lobbyists supplying information to them.
The statute sets a semiannual principal filing schedule and does not create any quarterly lobbyist-filed spending report.
Semiannual expense statements are required of registered principals, not lobbyists as named filers of a separate spending report.
The only periodic expense statement schedule is fixed to January 31 and July 31, not a tri-annual legislative-calendar schedule for lobbyists.

Itemized spending disclosure obligations in §13.68 attach to the principal’s expense statement; lobbyists only provide information to the principal and sign that information, not file their own itemized expense report.

The law requires principals to file semiannual expense statements and requires lobbyists to provide supporting information to the principal, so lobbyists do not file a separate spending report (cadence: none).
Identification of legislative proposals/topics is a reporting duty placed on the principal (as a condition of lobbying), not on the lobbyist as a separate filer of an activity/spending report.

Compensation to lobbyists is reported by the principal in its expense statement and may be itemized by lobbyist when exceeding $200, but the statute does not require the lobbyist to disclose earnings received from the principal in a lobbyist-filed report.
The statute requires the principal to keep and file a daily itemization of time spent lobbying, but it does not require lobbyists to disclose their contacts in a lobbyist-filed periodic report.
Time spent per legislative proposal/topic (10%+ of time) is disclosed by principals, not lobbyists, and is about time rather than expenditures per issue in a lobbyist-filed report.
General subjects/topics of lobbying communications are reported by the principal to the board, not by lobbyists as separate report filers.
Any requirement to report general lobbying topics is imposed on the principal (who must report topics with reasonable specificity), not on lobbyists as separate spend-report filers.

While §13.625 restricts providing things of pecuniary value, the periodic disclosure report required by §13.68 is filed by principals, so there is no lobbyist-filed report component requiring itemization of gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect lobbying costs are disclosed (if at all) in the principal’s expense statement; the statute does not require lobbyists to file a separate report disclosing indirect (non-compensation) costs.

Because lobbyists do not file their own itemized spending reports (principals file the expense statement and lobbyists only provide supporting information), the described 'YES/MODERATE' lobbyist-report regime is not required.

Lobbyist licensing applications are filed by the lobbyist, but the question is about lobbyist address/phone in a lobbyist spending report; the statute’s periodic spending report is filed by principals, not lobbyists.
The statute requires principals to report each legislative proposal/proposed administrative rule number or topic of lobbying communications, not lobbyists as separate filers.
Disclosures about the principal’s business activity/nature and purposes are required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

Lobbyist authorization is filed with the board but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report disclosing principal address/phone; principal identity and address are part of the principal’s own registration under §13.64.

The periodic expense statement is filed by the principal and the registry is based on principal registration, so the law does not require lobbyists to file a separate spending report listing all principals represented.
Reporting legislative proposal numbers/proposed administrative rule numbers is required of principals, not lobbyists as the named filer of a spending/activity report.

Compensation to lobbyists for lobbying is included in the principal’s aggregate total lobbying expenditures, but the lobbyist is not required to file a separate report disclosing direct lobbying costs.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in a separate lobbyist-filed spending report.

The statute creates principal-filed expense statements with lobbyist-provided supporting information rather than lobbyist-filed itemized spending reports, so the described requirement does not exist for lobbyists.
Because lobbyists are not required to file a periodic spending report at all, there is no statutory requirement for a lobbyist to file a 'no activity' report for a period.
The statute’s periodic disclosure is the principal’s expense statement and does not require any lobbyist-filed reporting of spending on household members of public officials.
Any itemization requirements occur within the principal’s expense statement (with lobbyist supporting info), and there is no separate lobbyist spending report that would be itemized.
